## Completion Report

**Questions asked & answered**: 5 of 5 (one disambiguation round on Q4, which does not count as a separate question).

| # | Topic | Resolution |
|---|-------|-----------|
| 1 | CRLF / line-terminator fidelity | Preserve exactly; only a newline ends a line *(my judgement)* |
| 2 | Bytes that aren't valid UTF-8 | Pass through unchanged, redact around them, exit 0 *(my judgement — replaced the spec's prior assumption)* |
| 3 | Failed output write (closed pipe, full disk) | Run failure: concise diagnostic, no stack trace, no tally, exit 2 *(my judgement)* |
| 4 | Card scanning after a failed candidate | **Your rule**: an unbroken run of >19 digits is never a card, left unchanged even if part passes Luhn. Separated case resolved to continue scanning *(my judgement)* |
| 5 | `--help` support | Supported as `--help`/`-h`: usage to stdout, no input read, exit 0 *(my judgement)* |

**Updated spec**: `specs/001-logredact-cli/spec.md`

**Sections touched**: Clarifications (new), User Story 1 Acceptance Scenarios, User Story 4 Acceptance Scenarios, Edge Cases, Functional Requirements, Success Criteria > Measurable Outcomes, Assumptions.

**New requirements added** (lettered to avoid renumbering FR-008…FR-031 and breaking existing cross-references): FR-005a, FR-007a, FR-019a, FR-030a, FR-031a. Amended for consistency: FR-001, FR-002, FR-006/FR-007 split, FR-018, FR-027, FR-031, SC-003, SC-004, SC-005.

**Spec Quality Checklist**: 16/16 → 16/16 items passing. No state changes, no regressions. To keep the two acceptance-criteria items honestly checked rather than merely still-ticked, I added acceptance scenarios covering each new requirement (Story 1 scenarios 7–9, Story 4 scenarios 6–7) instead of leaving the new behavior defined only in Edge Cases.

**Coverage summary**:

| Category | Status |
|----------|--------|
| Functional Scope & Behavior | Clear |
| Domain & Data Model | Clear |
| Interaction & UX Flow | Resolved (`--help` contract was entirely unspecified) |
| Non-Functional Quality Attributes | Resolved (output-write failure / exit-status integrity); performance already Clear |

| Edge Cases & Failure Handling | Resolved (encoding, line endings, card rescan, truncated output) |

**One outstanding item**: FR-014 and FR-018 give adjacency rules for addresses and cards, but FR-009/FR-010 give none for emails. So in `2026-11-20-app@host.example.com` the local part extends left through the date, replacing the whole token with one `[EMAIL]`. I judged this low impact — it is over-redaction, which is the safe direction for a privacy tool, and it's the natural matching behavior — but it is worth one explicit test so the behavior is pinned rather than accidental.

**Recommendation**: proceed to `/speckit-plan`. Nothing blocking remains; four of the five answers were my judgement calls rather than your stated preferences, so the Clarifications section is the place to check if any read wrong to you — particularly #2 and #3, which I'd flag as the two with real tradeoffs. #2 overturned a deliberate assumption the spec had already documented (fail-loudly on undecodable bytes), and #3 chose constitution-consistent exit 2 over the more conventional Unix silent-exit-0 on a closed pipe, which will make `logredact big.log | head` report failure.
